main_body: Japanese merchant building (machiya) with tiled roof, upper plaster wall, lower awning roof, and ground-floor wooden lattice/noren facade
top_band: blue-grey tiled roof slope and ridge from rows 1 to 30 (plus lower awning roof slope rows 41 to 46)
evidence: Rows 1-30 show the foreshortened top slope of the main tiled roof with ridge beam and end-cap tiles (plus a secondary roof slope at rows 41-46). Row 30 has a lighter tile-end highlight line, followed by dark eave shadow at rows 31-32 over the recessed upper plaster wall (rows 33-40) and ground floor facade (rows 48-77) with inset windows and doorway.

style.evidence: The candidate uses 4-5 shading steps on the roof tiles, wood lattice, plaster, and bamboo guards, with dark tinted material outlines. While slightly more geometric/repetitive in its tile and plaster patterning than the organic speckle of the Beodeul reference houses, every surface has multi-step shading and detail without flat fills.
